architecture_design_principles.title: Sampling should follow localized solution complexity
recommendations: residual_based_adaptive_refinement
retain_uniform_refresh
retain_initial_boundary_anchors
risks: Adaptive sampling may collapse around one residual hotspot.
tradeoffs: Higher local resolution adds refinement and evaluation cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Incompressible velocity-pressure balance
recommendations: balance momentum and divergence constraints
risks: Pressure and velocity losses can be poorly conditioned.
tradeoffs: Constraint accuracy competes with optimization conditioning.

architecture_design_principles.title: Local capacity for persistent shock-region error
recommendations: increase registered local representation capacity or sampling resolution only where measured shock-region error persists
risks: Global capacity growth may waste budget without improving the localized error.
tradeoffs: Local resolution competes with global coverage and parameter cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Smooth derivative-compatible representation
recommendations: choose smooth activations
match automatic-differentiation stability to PDE derivative order
risks: Non-smooth or poorly conditioned derivatives can dominate residual error.
tradeoffs: Smoother representations may trade local expressivity for stable differentiation.

architecture_design_principles.title: Capacity, conditioning, and cost balance
recommendations: use sufficient network capacity while preserving optimizer conditioning and fixed-budget cost
risks: Excess capacity can worsen conditioning and consume the fixed budget.
tradeoffs: Expressivity, trainability, and computational cost must be balanced.

architecture_design_principles.title: Cross-module compatibility
recommendations: coordinate sampling, loss weighting, constraints, and optimization instead of changing one module in isolation
risks: Individually reasonable modules can form an unstable combination.
tradeoffs: Joint changes improve compatibility but make attribution harder.

architecture_design_principles.title: Preserve useful gradient flow
recommendations: coordinate network conditioning, learning rate, and loss balance to preserve useful gradients
risks: Competing residual terms can suppress physically important gradients.
tradeoffs: Gradient protection may reduce aggressive short-term convergence.

architecture_design_principles.title: Evidence-bound architectural complexity
recommendations: add network, sampling, loss, or optimization complexity only when a physical feature or measured failure justifies it
risks: Unjustified modules consume budget and complicate failure attribution.
tradeoffs: Conservative complexity control can limit exploratory novelty.

architecture_design_principles.title: Initial-condition anchoring and constraint-first training
recommendations: strengthen initial-condition loss or a registered hard output transform
consider constraint-first or causal staging
risks: Overweighting the initial condition can slow interior residual reduction.
tradeoffs: Initial fidelity competes with later-time optimization progress.

architecture_design_principles.title: Protect optimization from high-order derivative instability
recommendations: reduce high-order residual weight
use conservative learning rates or gradient clipping
stage derivative terms when supported
risks: A warning raises attention; it does not recommend repeating the failed combination.
tradeoffs: Stability protection can slow convergence of higher-order constraints.

architecture_design_principles.title: Frequency-matched wave representation
recommendations: select a registered smooth representation with enough frequency bandwidth
control phase error
risks: Excessive feature frequency can destabilize derivatives.
tradeoffs: Spectral expressivity competes with derivative conditioning.

architecture_design_principles.title: Causal or time-segmented training
recommendations: consider registered causal weighting or time curricula when long-time error propagation is observed
risks: Time segmentation can create interface or curriculum bias.
tradeoffs: Causal focus improves temporal consistency at added scheduling cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Poisson interior-boundary coverage
recommendations: cover both domain interior and boundary
use a smooth representation for second derivatives
risks: Boundary or interior coverage gaps affect the global elliptic solution.
tradeoffs: Boundary density and interior coverage share the sampling budget.

architecture_design_principles.title: Moving-structure representation and phase control
recommendations: represent transported or high-frequency structure
anchor the initial profile
sample along moving error regions when justified
risks: Do not enable shock-specific refinement without shock or steep-gradient evidence.
tradeoffs: Tracking movement increases sampling complexity.

architecture_design_principles.title: Stiff multiscale optimization protection
recommendations: balance residual scales
use conservative learning-rate schedules
consider staged optimization
risks: Fast modes can dominate gradients and destabilize slow-mode learning.
tradeoffs: Stable schedules may need more iterations within the fixed budget.

architecture_design_principles.title: Reaction and diffusion loss balance
recommendations: monitor and balance reaction and diffusion residual contributions
risks: A single aggregate residual can hide one failed physical process.
tradeoffs: Adaptive balancing introduces additional optimization dynamics.

architecture_design_principles.title: Match representation to multiscale physical spectrum
recommendations: use a registered multiscale or frequency-aware network representation whose derivative conditioning remains stable
risks: Poorly chosen frequency scales can alias or destabilize derivatives.
tradeoffs: Broader spectral capacity increases model and conditioning cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Diverse early representation and sampling exploration
recommendations: explore materially different registered representations and sampling strategies
risks: Exploration consumes evaluations without guaranteed short-term gain.
tradeoffs: Diversity competes with immediate exploitation.

architecture_design_principles.title: Evidence-preserving late local refinement
recommendations: preserve measured strengths and make targeted cost-aware corrections
risks: Over-exploitation can miss a better design region.
tradeoffs: Local attribution and cost control reduce novelty.

architecture_design_principles.title: Constraint-preserving stagnation escape
recommendations: introduce a different representation or sampling principle while preserving physical constraints and avoiding failed complete combinations
risks: Large changes can discard useful measured structure.
tradeoffs: Escaping a local optimum sacrifices short-term continuity.

architecture_design_principles.title: Wave displacement-velocity dual initial enforcement
recommendations: retain both registered initial-displacement and time-derivative constraints
balance their scales before long-time interior fitting
consider initial-state pretraining when registered
risks: Optimizing displacement alone leaves the second-order evolution under-constrained.
tradeoffs: Stronger dual anchoring uses iterations that would otherwise reduce interior residuals.

architecture_design_principles.title: Local-frequency representation for heterogeneous waves
recommendations: use a registered smooth frequency-aware representation with bounded scales
sample coefficient-transition and slow-wave regions
retain global space-time coverage
risks: One aggressive global frequency scale can destabilize derivatives and miss local wavelength variation.
tradeoffs: Local spectral resolution increases feature and sampling cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Boundary-component stratification for complex geometry
recommendations: allocate boundary samples across every registered component
retain points near corners, holes, and narrow passages
keep interior samples out of excluded geometry
risks: Area-proportional sampling can starve a small but globally important boundary component.
tradeoffs: Boundary stratification reduces the interior share of a fixed sample budget.

architecture_design_principles.title: Coefficient-aware flux and transition sampling
recommendations: cover every coefficient regime
refine coefficient-gradient or interface regions when residual evidence supports it
monitor coefficient-weighted derivative terms separately
risks: Residual-only refinement may follow solution amplitude and ignore coefficient transitions.
tradeoffs: Coefficient-aware anchors consume points before posterior residual refinement.

architecture_design_principles.title: High-dimensional low-discrepancy sampling and factorized capacity
recommendations: prefer registered low-discrepancy sampling over tensor grids
consider factorized or parameter-efficient registered networks
reserve explicit boundary and initial coverage
risks: Dense grids scale exponentially and oversized dense networks exhaust the fixed budget.
tradeoffs: Factorization lowers cost but can impose an insufficient low-rank bias.

architecture_design_principles.title: Coupled state-parameter inverse optimization
recommendations: track state and inferred-parameter objectives separately
use registered component-aware weighting or optimizer grouping
stage refinement only when joint optimization is ill-conditioned
risks: A flexible state network can absorb error and leave the physical parameter unidentified.
tradeoffs: Parameter-specific optimization improves control but adds scheduling complexity.

architecture_design_principles.title: Noise-robust observation and physics balance
recommendations: consider a registered robust observation loss
avoid repeatedly sampling a few noisy observations as if independent
balance data and PDE terms using component diagnostics
risks: Aggressive data fitting transfers observation noise into the inferred field or parameter.
tradeoffs: Robust losses reduce outlier influence but may discard genuinely informative extremes.

architecture_design_principles.title: Conservative shallow-water component balance
recommendations: retain mass and both momentum residual components
use registered component-aware weighting
audit global mass and per-equation residuals
risks: A summed loss can hide a failed momentum equation or slow mass drift.
tradeoffs: Component balancing may slow the easiest equation while protecting the coupled solution.

architecture_design_principles.title: Positivity-preserving water-depth output
recommendations: prefer the registered positive-channel hard transform when its conditioning is acceptable
otherwise retain explicit positivity loss and violation metrics
scale depth and momentum consistently
risks: A saturating positive transform can create vanishing gradients near the minimum depth.
tradeoffs: Hard admissibility improves safety but can make conservative residual optimization stiffer.

architecture_design_principles.title: Periodic space-time sampling for shallow-water propagation
recommendations: retain paired periodic constraints in both spatial directions
anchor the initial conservative state
use global time coverage with causal refinement only when errors propagate
risks: Unpaired boundary sampling creates artificial sources or sinks at the periodic seam.
tradeoffs: Periodic pairs and initial anchors reduce freely adaptive interior samples.

architecture_design_principles.title: Poisson-Boltzmann nonlinear elliptic balancing
recommendations: use a smooth derivative-compatible activation
track curvature and nonlinear screening contributions
sample nonlinear hotspots and all hole boundaries
use conservative optimization before quasi-Newton refinement
risks: Large nonlinear responses can dominate gradients and destabilize second derivatives.
tradeoffs: Residual decomposition improves conditioning diagnostics but adds balancing dynamics.

architecture_design_principles.title: Darcy coefficient-weighted flux resolution
recommendations: use a smooth second-derivative-compatible representation
cover high-conductivity and high-coefficient-gradient regions
monitor coefficient-weighted flux residual
use registered exact boundary enforcement when stable
risks: Uniform sampling and pressure-only diagnostics can miss localized flux error.
tradeoffs: Flux-focused resolution increases derivative cost and may reduce uniform interior density.

architecture_design_principles.title: Smooth periodic representation for fourth-order KS dynamics
recommendations: use a registered smooth activation and periodic-compatible frequency representation
avoid nonsmooth activations for fourth derivatives
enforce periodic value and relevant derivative consistency
risks: High-frequency features can make fourth derivatives numerically explosive.
tradeoffs: Stronger smoothness and bounded frequencies improve derivatives but may limit chaotic mode capacity.

architecture_design_principles.title: Short-to-long horizon curriculum for chaotic dynamics
recommendations: establish early-time trajectory accuracy before expanding the time horizon
retain earlier windows during expansion
monitor time-slice and spectral diagnostics
risks: A moving window that forgets early states can create discontinuous or phase-shifted trajectories.
tradeoffs: Causal horizon expansion uses more scheduling overhead within the fixed iteration budget.

architecture_design_principles.title: Early-time multiscale heat resolution
recommendations: use a bounded registered multiscale representation
increase early-time resolution while retaining full-horizon samples
balance high- and low-frequency error
risks: Aggressive frequencies can destabilize second derivatives; late-only sampling misses rapidly decaying modes.
tradeoffs: Early high-frequency fidelity consumes capacity that may be unnecessary at late times.

architecture_design_principles.title: Amplitude-aware long-time loss and sampling
recommendations: stratify samples across the full time horizon
use registered normalized or adaptive weighting when time-slice scales differ
retain initial and late-time diagnostics
risks: Raw aggregate loss may ignore low-amplitude late states or overfocus a difficult final slice.
tradeoffs: Time-stratified balancing can slow convergence on the dominant interval.

architecture_design_principles.title: Reaction-diffusion interface and pattern refinement
recommendations: use residual or gradient adaptive sampling around measured fronts or pattern boundaries
retain uniform refresh and initial anchors
monitor both coupled fields
risks: Premature refinement can chase transient residual noise instead of physical interfaces.
tradeoffs: Local pattern resolution reduces global sample coverage.

architecture_design_principles.title: Pressure-gauge and flow-component control
recommendations: retain the registered pressure anchor
balance gauge, divergence, and momentum terms
monitor pressure offset separately from gradients
risks: A single fixed gauge point can be numerically overwhelmed by dense residual batches.
tradeoffs: Gauge protection adds another scale to multi-component loss balancing.

architecture_design_principles.title: Two-sided interface transmission sampling
recommendations: sample both sides of each registered interface
retain state and flux transmission terms
use component diagnostics before residual-adaptive concentration
risks: One-sided points can make a discontinuous coefficient appear smooth while violating flux continuity.
tradeoffs: Explicit interface pairs consume boundary-budget capacity.

architecture_design_principles.title: Constraint-type and derivative-order matching
recommendations: match the representation smoothness to every registered derivative-valued condition
retain separate diagnostics for value and derivative constraints
use hard transforms only when registered for the exact condition
risks: A hard transform for one condition can make another derivative constraint poorly conditioned.
tradeoffs: Constraint-specific diagnostics add loss components but expose hidden failures.

architecture_design_principles.title: Periodic-compatible coordinate representation
recommendations: consider registered periodic or bounded Fourier coordinate features
pair periodic samples exactly
preserve derivative smoothness at the seam
risks: Unbounded or excessive frequencies amplify derivative noise.
tradeoffs: Built-in periodicity reduces boundary mismatch but constrains the representation basis.

architecture_design_principles.title: Component-wise equation and state normalization
recommendations: record per-equation and per-output scales
use registered normalized, LRA, NTK, or component-aware weighting when imbalance is measured
avoid one shared scalar diagnostic
risks: Rapidly changing adaptive weights can destabilize coupled training.
tradeoffs: Component protection can slow convergence of the numerically easiest field.

architecture_design_principles.title: Diagnostic-driven sampler mixture
recommendations: combine a global low-discrepancy or uniform base with adaptive residual or gradient points
retain boundary and initial anchors
refresh adaptively only after reliable diagnostics exist
risks: A purely adaptive pool can collapse around transient noise or one equation component.
tradeoffs: Maintaining exploration points reduces maximum concentration at the current hotspot.

architecture_design_principles.title: Condition-aware optimizer phase handoff
recommendations: use first-order optimization to establish a stable basin
switch to registered quasi-Newton refinement only after losses and constraints are finite and balanced
preserve the fixed total iteration budget
risks: Premature quasi-Newton optimization can amplify noisy or badly scaled derivatives.
tradeoffs: A conservative handoff leaves fewer iterations for final refinement.

architecture_design_principles.title: Hard-versus-soft constraint conditioning
recommendations: use only problem-registered hard transforms
compare transform derivative conditioning against soft-penalty imbalance
retain diagnostics even for exactly enforced constraints
risks: A hard transform can satisfy the boundary while shrinking useful interior gradients.
tradeoffs: Exact satisfaction removes one optimization objective but restricts the function class.

architecture_design_principles.title: Vector and periodic design for two-dimensional Burgers
recommendations: use shared capacity with component diagnostics or a registered parallel output network
pair periodic points in both axes
refine component-specific shock residuals without dropping global points
risks: Independent output branches can lose cross-advection coupling if loss balance is weak.
tradeoffs: Parallel capacity reduces component interference at higher parameter cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Allen-Cahn front, phase-bound, and energy design
recommendations: use a smooth representation with enough local front capacity
mix global points with residual or gradient refinement near the front
monitor overshoot and stage stiff residual optimization
risks: Front-only refinement can lose correct bulk phase values.
tradeoffs: Narrow-interface resolution requires capacity and points that are redundant in bulk regions.

architecture_design_principles.title: Gray-Scott species and pattern-spectrum design
recommendations: consider a registered multiscale or Fourier representation with bounded frequencies
balance both species and reaction-diffusion terms
stratify time and refine measured pattern boundaries
use a causal horizon schedule
risks: High-frequency capacity can fit residual noise while losing stable pattern scale.
tradeoffs: Pattern expressivity and long-horizon staging consume substantial fixed-budget capacity.

architecture_design_principles.title: Space-time coefficient-stratified heat sampling
recommendations: stratify samples over coefficient extrema and time
retain dense initial anchors
track coefficient-weighted diffusion separately from the time derivative
risks: Uniform space-time sampling may underrepresent small regions with extreme diffusion rate.
tradeoffs: Coefficient strata reduce freely adaptive residual points.

architecture_design_principles.title: Complex heat geometry and Robin boundary design
recommendations: use smooth activations for normal derivatives
stratify samples by hole and outer boundary
diagnose Robin value and flux contributions separately
retain time coverage on every boundary component
risks: Combining all Robin residuals can hide one misoriented or under-sampled boundary component.
tradeoffs: Boundary-component balance reduces interior sample density.

architecture_design_principles.title: Radial low-discrepancy design for five-dimensional heat
recommendations: use geometry-valid low-discrepancy interior and surface samples
consider a registered factorized network
retain normal-derivative boundary diagnostics
avoid tensor grids
risks: Naive normalization of box samples can bias the radial distribution.
tradeoffs: Geometry-aware sampling is less flexible than unconstrained box sampling.

architecture_design_principles.title: Long-time wave phase and amplitude control
recommendations: normalize the full input bounds
use a bounded registered frequency representation that can resolve 50 temporal cycles
retain separate initial-displacement, initial-velocity, and spatial-boundary constraints
prefer a scale-normalized separable space-time representation when the registered wave modes share one temporal frequency
use scale-aware output parameterization and normalize physical residual magnitudes for the O(sinh(3*pi)) reference amplitude
monitor time-slice phase and amplitude
combine constraint-fitting warmup with stable PDE refinement
risks: An excessively narrow frequency basis locks in phase bias; an overly broad basis destabilizes derivatives.
Applying the full raw-scale PDE penalty before the large-amplitude constraints are represented can favor the trivial zero solution.
A separable temporal representation is invalid when registered modes have different temporal frequencies.
tradeoffs: Long-horizon phase control requires more temporal strata and diagnostic overhead.

architecture_design_principles.title: Coefficient-aware heterogeneous-wave encoding
recommendations: use registered coordinate features that can resolve local wavelength variation
sample coefficient-gradient regions
track phase error by coefficient regime
retain Dirichlet and Neumann boundary diagnostics
risks: Treating coefficient variation as a single global scale biases travel time and refraction.
tradeoffs: Coefficient-aware resolution increases representation complexity without adding new physical inputs.

architecture_design_principles.title: Lid-driven cavity wall and corner refinement
recommendations: stratify moving-lid, stationary-wall, and corner samples
balance wall, divergence, momentum, and pressure-gauge terms
use residual refinement only after wall constraints stabilize
risks: Residual adaptation before wall convergence can chase artificial corner errors.
tradeoffs: Wall-focused sampling leaves fewer points in the vortex core.

architecture_design_principles.title: Backward-step shear-layer and reattachment refinement
recommendations: retain geometry-stratified wall and step samples
refine the measured shear layer and reattachment region
balance reverse-flow velocity, momentum, and divergence diagnostics
risks: Global residual refinement may neglect the thin separated shear layer.
tradeoffs: Local recirculation resolution increases evaluation and sampling cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Long-time Navier-Stokes vorticity curriculum
recommendations: expand the time horizon while retaining earlier samples
balance momentum, divergence, initial, and boundary components
track derivative-sensitive vorticity diagnostics
risks: Late-window fitting can repair velocity values while retaining accumulated divergence error.
tradeoffs: Vorticity-aware diagnostics and causal staging consume fixed-budget iterations.

architecture_design_principles.title: Kovasznay mixed spatial modes and output balance
recommendations: use a smooth representation capable of exponential and oscillatory spatial modes
balance velocity, pressure, divergence, and gauge components
retain full analytic boundary coverage
risks: One shared output scale can underfit pressure while velocities converge.
tradeoffs: Component-specific capacity improves balance at added parameter cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Partition-stratified sampling for many-area Poisson
recommendations: allocate interior points to every subdomain
sample both sides of interfaces and multi-subdomain junctions
separate external Robin and internal transmission losses
consider registered multiscale features
risks: Residual-proportional allocation can starve easy-looking subdomains that transmit global bias.
tradeoffs: Guaranteed partition coverage reduces concentration on the worst current interface.

architecture_design_principles.title: Three-dimensional Neumann geometry and nullspace design
recommendations: use smooth activations for second and normal derivatives
stratify outer and hole surfaces
sample both coefficient regions
preserve any registered normalization and monitor offset
risks: Surface undercoverage or nullspace drift can dominate state MSE.
tradeoffs: Surface and interface coverage significantly reduces the 3D interior budget.

architecture_design_principles.title: Projection-aware five-dimensional Poisson design
recommendations: use registered low-discrepancy sampling
consider factorized capacity
track derivative residuals by coordinate
audit random low-dimensional projections in addition to global metrics
risks: A model can fit dominant coordinate directions and neglect weaker ones.
tradeoffs: Coordinate-wise diagnostics add cost but expose anisotropic failure.

architecture_design_principles.title: Inverse Poisson sensor-to-physics design
recommendations: track state, inferred quantity, data, PDE, and boundary objectives separately
use registered robust observation loss when justified
avoid duplicating fixed noisy sensors
stage state and parameter refinement only after diagnosing imbalance
risks: The state network can interpolate sensors while the inferred field is wrong between them.
tradeoffs: Separate inverse diagnostics increase optimization complexity.

architecture_design_principles.title: Inverse heat temporal-sensor design
recommendations: stratify PDE samples around observation times while retaining full-horizon coverage
balance early and late sensor information
use robust data loss and component-aware parameter optimization
monitor extrapolation between sensor times
risks: Overconcentration at sensor times can produce poor dynamics between observations.
tradeoffs: Temporal sensor stratification reduces unconstrained adaptive sampling.

architecture_design_principles.title: Shallow-water characteristic and state scaling
recommendations: scale depth and momentum using registered physical ranges without changing the PDE
balance mass and momentum residuals
pair positivity enforcement with conservative diagnostics
risks: Poor scaling makes momentum gradients dominate depth positivity or vice versa.
tradeoffs: Physical scaling improves conditioning but requires an explicit reversible mapping.

architecture_design_principles.title: Poisson-Boltzmann hole-boundary hotspot design
recommendations: stratify all four hole boundaries
refine regions where nonlinear screening and curvature are jointly large
use smooth bounded-capacity representations
balance nonlinear and derivative residual contributions
risks: Residual refinement can collapse around one hole and leave others underresolved.
tradeoffs: Per-hole coverage reduces the points available to the strongest nonlinear hotspot.

architecture_design_principles.title: Darcy energy and flux diagnostic design
recommendations: track state, gradient, coefficient-weighted flux, and boundary errors
use coefficient-stratified samples
apply stable first-to-second-order optimizer handoff
risks: State-MSE-driven selection can prefer a model with inferior physical flux.
tradeoffs: Derivative diagnostics add evaluation cost but improve physical candidate ranking.

architecture_design_principles.title: Viscous-shock design for one-dimensional Burgers
recommendations: use smooth local capacity
retain initial and endpoint anchors
mix global points with shock-region residual or gradient refinement
balance convection and diffusion residual behavior
risks: Overly aggressive local features can oscillate near the shock or destabilize second derivatives.
tradeoffs: Shock resolution uses capacity and samples that contribute little in smooth regions.

architecture_design_principles.title: Dynamic-range balancing for long-time heat
recommendations: stratify early, middle, and late times
consider registered normalized weighting across time slices
retain strong initial anchoring
delay quasi-Newton refinement until slice losses are balanced
risks: Normalizing very small late states can overamplify noise or numerical error.
tradeoffs: Protecting the long tail slows reduction of large early-time errors.

architecture_design_principles.title: Directional multiscale features for anisotropic heat
recommendations: use bounded registered multiscale features that cover both spatial directions
sample densely near the initial transient
track directional derivative and frequency errors
retain low-frequency capacity
risks: Isotropic frequency features can waste capacity in one direction and underresolve the other.
tradeoffs: Directional feature coverage increases feature dimension and derivative cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Hole-aware sampling for classic two-dimensional Poisson
recommendations: stratify outer and hole boundaries
add near-boundary interior points
use smooth second-derivative-compatible capacity
keep a global low-discrepancy interior base
risks: Uniform boundary sampling can undersample a small curved hole.
tradeoffs: Near-hole refinement reduces bulk interior density.

architecture_design_principles.title: Modal representation and dual-initial pretraining for wave_1d
recommendations: use a bounded registered Fourier or sine-capable representation
pretrain both initial constraints when registered
retain spatial-boundary anchors
transition gradually to full PDE optimization
risks: Excessive initial pretraining can create a basin that fits the initial slice but propagates poorly.
tradeoffs: Dual-initial pretraining consumes iterations before interior residual training.

architecture_design_principles.title: Characteristic-aware hyperbolic sampling
recommendations: retain global coverage while refining moving fronts
stratify inflow, outflow, and initial data
use causal windows when registered
risks: Static residual hotspots may lag behind moving characteristic structure.
tradeoffs: Front tracking adds sampling complexity and evaluation cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Conservative-state design for compressible flow
recommendations: predict or consistently derive registered conservative variables
balance mass, momentum, and energy components
monitor primitive-state admissibility
risks: Independent output scales can violate the equation of state.
tradeoffs: Conservative coupling improves physics but increases multi-component conditioning difficulty.

architecture_design_principles.title: Entropy and weak-residual design for shocks
recommendations: retain conservative residual components
add registered entropy or weak diagnostics
sample both sides of discontinuities
risks: Strong derivatives at a shock can dominate optimization without selecting the admissible branch.
tradeoffs: Weak or entropy diagnostics introduce integration and quadrature cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Admissible positive state for compressible flow
recommendations: use only registered positive-state transforms or penalties
monitor minimum density and pressure
scale conservative variables consistently
risks: Saturating transforms can produce vanishing gradients near vacuum.
tradeoffs: Hard admissibility improves safety but may stiffen flux optimization.

architecture_design_principles.title: Contact-discontinuity resolution without shock overregularization
recommendations: diagnose contact and shock regions separately
use local refinement with uniform refresh
avoid entropy penalties on pure contacts unless physically justified
risks: Shock-oriented regularization can smear transported material interfaces.
tradeoffs: Wave-type-specific treatment adds classification and sampling overhead.

architecture_design_principles.title: Boundary-layer multiscale coordinates and sampling
recommendations: use bounded multiscale features or problem-registered coordinate transforms
stratify layer and outer regions
balance layer and global errors
risks: Aggressive layer coordinates can damage derivative conditioning outside the layer.
tradeoffs: Layer resolution consumes capacity that is redundant in the outer domain.

architecture_design_principles.title: Tensor-aligned anisotropic representation
recommendations: align resolution with registered tensor principal directions when available
sample strong-gradient directions
track tensor-weighted flux components
risks: Using inferred directions as immutable physics can bias the model.
tradeoffs: Directional features reduce isotropic flexibility.

architecture_design_principles.title: Degenerate-diffusion front and positivity design
recommendations: use registered nonnegative output enforcement
refine the moving support boundary
retain zero-region and active-region samples
track nonlinear flux
risks: Smooth activations may create nonphysical low-amplitude tails outside support.
tradeoffs: Support sharpness and derivative smoothness compete.

architecture_design_principles.title: Porous-medium mass and support control
recommendations: stratify time and moving-front neighborhoods
monitor global mass
retain positivity and zero-state diagnostics
expand the horizon causally
risks: Front-focused sampling can allow global mass drift.
tradeoffs: Mass and support objectives add competing scales.

architecture_design_principles.title: Elliptic nullspace and gauge control
recommendations: retain registered gauge, mean, or anchor constraints
separate energy and offset errors
prevent dense residuals from overwhelming nullspace control
risks: Optimizer drift along a flat null direction can destabilize otherwise accurate fields.
tradeoffs: Nullspace constraints add a global loss scale.

architecture_design_principles.title: Mixed-boundary stratified constraints
recommendations: stratify samples by boundary subset and operator type
use smooth activations for derivative conditions
record per-subset residuals
risks: Area-weighted aggregation can starve a small high-impact boundary subset.
tradeoffs: Guaranteed subset coverage reduces adaptive interior points.

architecture_design_principles.title: Local enrichment near singular sources
recommendations: separate near-singular and regular regions
use supported weak or integral diagnostics
retain global coverage and source-strength constraints
risks: Direct high-order autodiff at a singularity may be undefined or unstable.
tradeoffs: Local enrichment complicates architecture and attribution.

architecture_design_principles.title: Mixed displacement-stress elasticity design
recommendations: use shared or registered parallel capacity for mechanical fields
balance equilibrium, constitutive, displacement, and traction terms
track stress symmetry
risks: Independent stress and displacement branches can violate compatibility.
tradeoffs: Mixed variables lower derivative order but increase outputs and constraints.

architecture_design_principles.title: Traction boundary and rigid-mode control
recommendations: stratify displacement and traction boundaries
retain registered rigid-motion anchors
use smooth representations for stress derivatives
risks: Traction-only training can drift in rigid modes.
tradeoffs: Anchors select uniqueness but must not overconstrain deformation.

architecture_design_principles.title: Mixed pressure design for nearly incompressible solids
recommendations: use a registered mixed pressure-displacement form when available
balance volumetric and deviatoric components
monitor volume change and stress
risks: Poor pressure coupling produces locking or spurious pressure modes.
tradeoffs: Mixed formulation adds an output and saddle-like optimization.

architecture_design_principles.title: Curl-compatible electromagnetic representation
recommendations: use smooth vector-field capacity compatible with curl derivatives
balance electric and magnetic components
match frequency bandwidth to the physical spectrum
risks: Component-wise scalar networks can learn incompatible vector structure.
tradeoffs: Vector-compatible coupling increases architecture complexity.

architecture_design_principles.title: Electromagnetic divergence control
recommendations: retain Gauss constraints alongside curl equations
use component-aware weighting
monitor divergence drift across time
risks: Curl residuals may converge while divergence error accumulates.
tradeoffs: Divergence protection adds stiffness to time-dependent training.

architecture_design_principles.title: Two-sided electromagnetic interface sampling
recommendations: sample both material sides
separate tangential and normal transmission components
retain global wave coverage
risks: Single-sided interface points cannot identify the correct jump.
tradeoffs: Interface pairs reduce bulk samples.

architecture_design_principles.title: Wave energy, phase, and boundary-flux diagnostics
recommendations: stratify time slices
track phase, amplitude, and energy proxies
separate reflecting, absorbing, and forcing boundaries
risks: Pointwise MSE can hide coherent phase drift.
tradeoffs: Derived diagnostics add evaluation cost.

architecture_design_principles.title: Wavenumber-aware Helmholtz representation and curriculum
recommendations: use bounded registered frequency features
ensure domain sampling resolves wavelengths
consider low-to-target-frequency continuation when supported
delay quasi-Newton refinement until phase is stable
risks: Excess frequencies destabilize second derivatives; insufficient frequencies cause pollution.
tradeoffs: Frequency continuation adds stages within the fixed budget.

architecture_design_principles.title: Eigenmode normalization, orthogonality, and deflation
recommendations: include nontrivial normalization
use orthogonality or registered deflation for multiple modes
optimize eigenvalue and field jointly
audit residual by mode
